70 "convenience functions for reading RDL data from a file or a generic input "

72 "which reads binary data directly from byte strings assumes the framing has already "

75 "RDL framing is very simple, so if you want to handle it at a higher level and "

78 " +---------+---------+------------+------------+ \n"
79 " | mlen | plen | manifest | payload | \n"
80 " +---------+---------+------------+------------+ \n"

311 "A BinaryWriter object can decode a binary stream of RDL data into a SceneContext. "

315 "Since BinaryWriter doesn't need to make any modifications to the SceneContext, it can "

321 "SceneContext should work just fine. \n"

323 "The BinaryWriter can handle binary data to a number of sinks. There are "
324 "convenience functions for reading RDL data from a file or a generic input "
325 "stream. These methods handle proper framing of the RDL binary data. The method "
326 "which writes binary data directly to byte strings assumes the framing will be added later by the caller.\n"
327 "\n"
328 "RDL framing is very simple, so if you want to handle it at a higher level and "
329 "write directly into byte strings it's not very hard. The frame looks like this: \n"
330 "\n\n"
331 " +---------+---------+------------+------------+ \n"
332 " | mlen | plen | manifest | payload | \n"
333 " +---------+---------+------------+------------+ \n"
334 " | 8 bytes | 8 bytes | mlen bytes | plen bytes | \n"
335 " +---------+---------+------------+------------+ \n"
336 " ^-- first byte last byte --^ \n"
337 "\n\n"
338 "NOTE: Both mlen and plen are 64-bit unsigned integers, in network byte order (big endian). \n"
339 "\n"
340 "This encoding allows us to easily read the manifest and payload into separate buffers. "
341 "The manifest must be decoded serially, but once decoded, we have offsets into each message "
342 "in the payload, so we can decode it in parallel. \n"
343 "\n"
344 "Thread Safety: \n"
345 " - Since the BinaryWriter reads SceneContext data (in particular, SceneObjects), it is "

710 const std::string rdl2Mat3fDocString =
711 "3x3 Column Major Matrix (holding values of type float)"
712 "\n"
713 "NOTE: only basic functionality available in Python. If more is needed, open a JIRA "
714 "and submit a request."
715 "\n"
716 " Matrix formats can be confusing. When we say 'column major' it's only meaningful "
717 "when we are discussing it in certain context, such as transformations. We are not "
718 "referring to the underlying storage of the matrix data, which could be in any form "
719 "(arrays, vectors, etc.). Regardless of row major or column major, multiplications between "
720 "matrices do not change (multiply a row by a column)."
721 "\n"
722 " However, when we define transformations of point, vectors, etc., we need to be clear "
723 "about the meanings of the rows and columns of a matrix and their corresponding "
724 "multiplication with vectors."
725 "\n"
726 " DWA specifies the transformation matrix in column major, so vector transformation "
727 "is applied using post-multiply. Normal transformation is done using pre-multiply. "
728 "These are defined as follows."
729 "\n"
730 " 'Row vector' means vectors are defined as v = [x, y, z], also can be "
731 "considered as a 1 by n matrix, where n = 3."
732 "\n"
733 " 'Column vector' is the row vector transposed, which is a n by 1 matrix."
734 "\n"
735 " Matrix multiply for a row vector can be done by post-multiply, where the matrix "
736 "is after the row vector:"
737 "\n"
738 " u = v * M (equivalent to transpose(M) * transpose(v))"
739 "\n"
740 " Or it's possible to do pre-multiply, which implicitly transposes the vector v "
741 "into a column vector:"
742 "\n"
743 " w = M * v (where v is assumed to be a column vector)"
744 "\n"
745 " In general, u != w (note the missing transpose for M), because matrix "
746 "multiplication is not commutative."
747 "\n"
748 "The set of transform*() interface should be preferable over multiplication since "
749 "their intentions are unambiguous.";
750

123 "The SceneClass represents all the metadata and structure of SceneObjects of a particular type. "
124 "It is analogous to a C++ class for render objects that are declared at runtime."

126 "In addition to allowing the declaration of attributes, it also handles a lot of the messy "

130 "Once the SceneClass is 'complete', no more attribute declarations can occur. The SceneContext "

131 {
132 const std::string rdl2SceneContextDocstring =
133 "The SceneContext represents all the data for a specific scene in RDL. This "
134 "includes all the objects in the scene (SceneObjects) as well as their types "
135 "(SceneClasses). It provides some basic functionality for creating "
136 "SceneClasses and SceneObjects, iterating through them, finding them by their "
137 "unique name, and retreving them so you can query or update their attributes.\n"
138 "Once the data has been loaded or updated, the rendering libraries should be "
139 "given a immutable reference to the SceneContext. RDL makes heavy use of its const "
140 "correct API to indicate which methods and objects are read-only and thread "
141 "safe. If you stick to the const API and don't violate its integrity, it should "
142 "be completely safe to traverse the SceneContext and all its objects from multiple"
143 " threads concurrently.\n"
144 "Don't worry about calling createSceneClass() or createSceneObject() multiple "
145 "times by accident. They both have 'create if it does not exist' semantics, "
146 "and are effectively no-ops if the class or object exists. In the case of "
147 "createSceneObject, it will return the existing object.\n"
148 "Thread Safety:\n"
149 " - The only points of synchronization in the SceneContext are the SceneClass "
150 "and SceneObject hash maps. These control access to the hash map with reader/writer "
151 "locks, so it should only be slow in the presence of writers. Even then, it's only "
152 "slow while we're inserting the SceneClass or SceneObject into the hash table."
153 " Once the insertion is finished, the lock is released and you can continue updating"
154 " the object without holding the lock.\n"
155 " - SceneClasses and SceneObjects do not synchronize access to themselves, so "
156 "writing to these objects must only happen in a single thread. They are completely "
157 "self contained, though, so you are free to write to different SceneClasses or "
158 "SceneObjects in different threads concurrently.";
159

120 .def("update",
121 &rdl2::SceneVariables::update,
122 "update() is called automatically before rendering starts by RDL, whenever the "
123 "attributes or bindings of an object have changed (on this object or any of its "
124 "object-attributes or bindings). You should not have to manually call this "
125 "function on a scene object."
126 "\n"
127 "The update() method is to notify a derived class that the object has changed. "
128 "This method can be reimplemented by derived (DSO) object types to react to changes "
129 "in this objects attributes. This can be used for verifying that attribute data "
130 "is valid, or rebuilding cached data from attribute source data."
131 "\n"
132 "There may be changes to multiple attributes or bindings per single update() call. "
133 "You can find out which attributes or bindings changed using the hasChanged(AttributeKey) "
134 "and hasBindingChanged(AttributeKey) functions for the attributes in question."
135 "\n"
136 "When this function is called on a given object, you are guaranteed that it has already "
137 "been called on its dependencies, the tree (more accurately the directed acyclic graph) "
138 "of objects connected through attributes and bindings to this object. You have no guarantees, "
139 "however, about objects outside of this tree (graph). Though all objects may be accessible "
140 "through the SceneContext via the SceneClass, it is only safe to query the objects in "
141 "the dependency tree of the current object."
142 "\n"
143 "Note that currently update() will not be called on any additional objects based on "
144 "changes to SceneVariables."
145 "\n"
146 "RDL does not track attribute value history, so it cannot tell you what the "
147 "previous value was.")
